correctness.rationale: The precise two-period recurrences follow from the resolvent of a quarter-turn. Multiplying the complex state matrices gives the quoted traces and identical determinants. Exact Schur–Cohn gaps factor as positive prefactors times 1-4ab (current-scaled) or 1-(a+b)^2 (history-scaled). The corresponding monodromy has a simple -1 eigenvalue exactly at equality and one outside the unit disk beyond. Equal-history nonzero starting states cannot lie in the decaying eigenspace: their first-step ratio has unit modulus. The standalone SymPy checker reconstructs the algebra and 214 tests pass. No computation is treated as a proof of infinite iteration convergence.

originality.rationale: The closest published fixed-step skew result yields only the diagonal a=b case; the variable-step linesearch source defines the previous-step weighting but has no prescribed two-period sharp stability comparison. Additional periodic/alternating and equivalent complex-polynomial searches returned no mathematical statement that implies both thresholds. Schur–Cohn and basic Floquet multipliers are not themselves claimed as novel; an equivalent unindexed specialization is a remaining risk.

value.rationale: A canonical worst-case skew inclusion makes the interplay between the previous and current step weights mathematically consequential. Exact separate geometric- and arithmetic-mean stability thresholds explain when a stored-gradient convention preserves an unusually aggressive two-cycle and when it fails; they form a sharp diagnostic for numerical splitting design, not a contrived single-parameter numerical observation. The comparison is not a general convergence guarantee, but the precise boundary itself is a motivated structural fact.
